mona: FYI onboarding rwdx-7b-quant-int4. Hit a weird case with cold restore + long priming (~20k tokens) where outputs insert a repeating token sequence shortly after restore. Repro steps + logs below.

mona: Repro (minimal):
```
# serve with int4 snapshots enabled
RWD_MODEL=rwdx-7b-quant-int4 ./serve --quant=int4 --kv-restore=true --max-context=65536
# priming with ~20k tokens then continue
curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/generate -d '{"prompt":"[~20000 tokens] ...","max_new_tokens":1024,"seed":7}'
```

mona: Symptoms: first ~18-20k generated tokens match float32 baseline. After the KV snapshot boundary, generation inserts a short repeated fragment ("and then it was") several times and beam scores drop. Warm server (no restart) never shows this.

leo: Can you dump KV shard headers? looks like a boundary alignment issue with packed int4.

mona: Pasted small excerpt of KV load log: 
```
[KV] shard=5 load_ok=true entries=20480
[KV-VERIFY] idx=20479 pos=20479 tok=0x1f2a ok
[KV-VERIFY] idx=20480 pos=0 tok=0x0b3d MISMATCH
```

priya: Heh. That off-by-one at the shard boundary screams "tail packing". int4 writes two nibbles/byte; if we don't mask tail nibble after unpack, random 0x0f padding can be interpreted as a real value.

mona: Did a hexdump of the snapshot file. Here is a snippet (truncated):
```
00001f20: ... a2 1f 2a 0b 3d 0f 0f 0f 0f 0f 0f
00001f2c: ... a2 1f 2a 0b 3d 0f 0f 0f 0f 0f 0f
```

simon: Yep. See repeated 0x0f sequence. That looks like the writer pads with 0x0f nibbles to fill the final byte. The loader must consult the exact nibble_count to avoid treating pad as token.

leo: Was the snapshot produced by the new packer? or did it come from an older CLI that wrote different header fields?

mona: Snapshot produced by publish pipeline last week (CICD). The file header claims format_version=1. The int4 packer change landed after v1 but publish didn't bump version; compatibility shim didn't exist.

priya: Proposed fix: 1) Add explicit nibble_count to snapshot header; 2) change magic/version to v2 when packing int4; 3) loader should mask off tail nibble using nibble_count. Also add CRC32 to header to detect truncated writes.

leo: Agree. Also add a CI integration test: produce int4 snapshot, restore into fresh server, run token-level comparison against float baseline for contexts [4k, 16k, 32k] and multiple seeds. Fail CI if KL divergence > threshold or token-repeat frequency spikes.

ci-bot: Queued: rwdx-7b-quant-int4/kv-restore-check (run id CI-9991). Results ~10m.

mona: Quick mitigation: set KV_RESTORE=false for int4 snapshots in staging and prod-pool until we roll the compatibility bump. That keeps behaviour correct but increases cold-start latency.

simon: I added a small binary checker that scans the tail bytes for 0x0f patterns and compares expected nibble_count -> if mismatch, fail early. I'll attach PR in a bit.

ci-bot: CI-9991 finished: 1 failure. Logs: https://ci.internal/runs/9991 (summary: tail nibble mis-read for shard=5).

priya: Thanks. For the PR: include backward conversion for v1 headers (word_count -> nibble_count) so old snapshots can still be consumed safely. Also add a small compatibility test that simulates v1 files with int4 pack to ensure loader doesn't silently treat pads as tokens.

leo: Good call. Add telemetry: when a restore occurs, emit metric rwd.kv.restore.padding_mismatch and count mismatches + which model/quant. That will alert us to any remaining latent bad snapshots.

mona: Filing RW-ML-2101 to track: "int4 snapshot tail padding -> token insertion after KV restore". Assigning to simon/priya.

priya: PR opened: https://git.internal/rwd/p/pkr/+/4782 (header v2, nibble_count, crc32, loader mask, reg tests).

ci-bot: PR job queued for 4782.

leo: After PR merges, let's run regression across the fleet snapshots from last 2 weeks to detect potentially corrupted files. We should refuse to load any snapshot whose CRC fails or whose nibble_count mismatch occurs.

mona: Added note to onboarding checklist: "verify int4 snapshot restore across long-context handoffs (4k/16k/32k)".

priya: Will push a short postmortem if CI validates fix. For now, temporary wrinkle only impacts int4 cold-restores, warm serves unaffected.

mona: Thanks all. If anyone else sees odd short-repeat tokens after cold restarts with quantized models, drop logs here.
